binding_rows.DR-004: Before a non-terminal KO compare immediate prizes, remaining KOs, attacker sequence, gust, and retaliation.
binding_rows.DR-005: Prefer the shorter/robuster route with fewer uncertain pieces; do not maximize immediate Prize value alone.
binding_rows.DR-006: When the next attacker is not ready and the opponent has a faster credible route, develop, disrupt, or pivot instead of a cosmetic KO.
binding_rows.STR-001: Enumerate plausible target/attacker sequences and prefer shortest robust completion with acceptable retaliation.
binding_rows.STR-002: Avoid an unfavourable attacker-for-attacker trade unless terminal or it blocks the opponent's only win.
binding_rows.SF-001: prize_map_distance; minimize; enumerate target sequences and penalize inaccessible or low-confidence pieces; terminal override.
binding_rows.SF-002: immediate_ko_threat; minimize; exact public damage/HP/attack/target/access computation plus explicit opponent-belief boundary.
binding_rows.SF-004: next_attacker_ready; maximize; binary plus distance-to-threshold, not attacker count alone.
binding_rows.SF-005: backup_attacker_count; maximize; route-compatible attackers weighted by energy/recovery/accessibility.
binding_rows.SF-006: bench_liability; minimize; Prize value, gust access, spread thresholds, and role necessity.
binding_rows.SF-016: terminal_outcome; exact engine WDL; terminal override before heuristic features; value in {-1,0,1}.
binding_rows.AP-001: Do not start a losing Prize trade for a cosmetic KO.
binding_rows.AP-008: Do not optimize damage when it does not shorten the route or cross a decisive threshold.
binding_rows.AP-009: Do not assert unseen hand/deck/Prize identities from compatible actions.
binding_rows.AP-011: Raw option order is not strategy; require semantic permutation controls.
binding_rows.AP-013: Low deck count is not a deck-out proof without a complete route comparison.
binding_rows.RQ-004: Open P0: exact Mega Abomasnow routes versus each native anchor under natural deployment.
binding_rows.RQ-005: Open P1: held-out CABT ablation of prize distance, attacker readiness, and gust conversion.
binding_rows.RQ-009: Belief model remains a separate open question; B1 must not silently become hidden-state inference.

Those values may be used only by a separately labelled offline fixture evaluator. No native route arm is eligible until an independently reviewed runtime-compatible source for every route feature exists.

route_graph_limits.horizon: At most 4 public attacker/target transitions or the exact configured request budget, whichever is smaller; report pruned branches.
route_graph_limits.branching: Complete legal option set at each node; no first-N truncation. Public response classes must be declared by the native receipt or deterministic fixture.
route_graph_limits.resource_rule: Known visible counts are exact. Hidden slots remain unknown intervals; no card identity may be allocated to a hidden slot without a separate approved belief experiment.
route_graph_limits.terminal_rule: Read terminal_result before selection or route data. A forced terminal win dominates every heuristic route.
route_graph_limits.stop_rule: STOP is a real legal option only when the engine exposes it and the selection contract permits it; it receives a semantic action record and never acts as an implicit empty choice.
route_graph_limits.equivalence_rule: Equivalent semantic actions are compared by canonical semantic key. Non-equivalent ties return AMBIGUOUS rather than using option order.

formulations.name: Lexicographic robust route
formulations.material_difference: Strict worst-case route selection. One bad declared public response prevents a route from outranking a route that survives all declared responses, even when its nominal immediate Prize value is larger.
formulations.falsifiable_hypothesis: On sealed public successor fixtures, complete public route mapping with a worst-case retaliation guard selects the declared robust route and avoids AP-001/AP-008 decisions. A held-out native WDL hypothesis is deferred until a runtime-compatible route oracle and exact route-critical semantics are independently qualified; this arm must not activate on unsupported or incomplete semantics.
formulations.route_worlds: All declared public legal response classes in the sealed offline fixture are adversarial for robustness. Unknown response coverage is not silently assigned a probability; no successor class is read by PolicyV1 at runtime.

feature_definitions.worst_case_remaining_prize_turns: Maximum declared-response route distance to a terminal Prize win; UNKNOWN if any required edge depends on a Phase A PARTIAL effect.
feature_definitions.worst_case_required_unknown_or_unavailab: Maximum count of required cards/energy/attacker/effect transitions that are not publicly accessible or semantically proven.
feature_definitions.next_attacker_ready: Exact public binary threshold plus distance-to-threshold from SF-004; unknown is not ready.
feature_definitions.opponent_route_distance_after_action: Minimum publicly declared opponent terminal route length after the candidate action; unknown response coverage is a robustness failure, not a favourable estimate.
feature_definitions.bench_liability: Public Prize value, gust exposure, spread threshold and role necessity from SF-006; partial effect dependencies are unknown.
feature_definitions.resource_reserve: Publicly countable route-compatible energy, recovery, evolution and gust reserve, with inaccessible copies excluded.

formulations.expected_behavior: Choose the lower-Prize or denial line when it has the shorter robust completion, reject cosmetic KOs without a ready follow-up, and choose a forced terminal action first.

formulations.name: Finite public-response completion route
formulations.material_difference: Expected-route selection over a fixed, explicitly declared public response envelope. A higher-mean line can beat a robust line when its response classes and weights are fully public and its tail remains above the fail threshold; this is not hidden-card belief.
formulations.falsifiable_hypothesis: On sealed public successor fixtures, a finite public response envelope can select a higher-mean route than A in states where A is overly conservative, while passing the declared tail guard. A held-out native WDL hypothesis is deferred until a runtime-compatible route oracle and exact route-critical semantics are independently qualified. If public response weights are missing, B is fixture-inactive rather than inventing them.
formulations.route_worlds: Only synthetic fixture classes with a sealed, predeclared weight are allowed in this first implementation. A future native arm may add public successor classes only after a separately reviewed runtime-compatible oracle is available. Weights are configuration/receipt inputs, not estimates of unseen hand or Prize identities. Every class must be public-state complete through the bounded horizon.

feature_definitions.expected_route_completion_score: Predeclared-weight mean over finite public classes of terminal completion score, with terminal win=1, draw=0.5 and loss=0 only when the public successor receipt reaches a terminal result; otherwise a normalized bounded route-completion score is used and labelled proxy.
feature_definitions.probability_of_no_catastrophic_public_re: Weight of classes whose bounded response does not expose a proven immediate loss or AP-001 retaliation; UNKNOWN is forbidden in B's active set.
feature_definitions.lower_tail_route_completion_score_at_10t: Weighted lower-tail score over the same public classes; it prevents the mean from hiding a declared catastrophic tail.
feature_definitions.expected_remaining_prize_turns: Predeclared-weight mean of complete public route distances, not a hidden-belief estimate.

formulations.expected_behavior: Choose a higher-mean route only when all public classes, weights and bounded successors are present and the tail guard passes; otherwise return UNRESOLVED and leave B0 control authority in place.

decision_output_contract.record: RouteDecisionV1 (design contract only; no implementation in this report)
fields: status: SELECTED, NO_SAFE_ROUTE, AMBIGUOUS, UNSUPPORTED, B0_DELEGATE, TERMINAL_OVERRIDE
formulation_id and authority: EXPERIMENTAL_PUBLIC_ROUTE or B0_CONTROL
chosen_semantic_action_key and chosen_option_fingerprints; never chosen raw index as authority
decision_key with named values, units, source and known/unknown status
route_activation_id and route_key_sha256 for trace joining

status_rules.TERMINAL_OVERRIDE: Evaluator-only status after an exact engine terminal check identifies a terminal win/draw/loss; the PolicyV1 runtime never receives a terminal selection request and must not claim this status for a current action.
status_rules.SELECTED: Only if all features needed by the selected key are public, complete and non-ambiguous within horizon.
status_rules.NO_SAFE_ROUTE: No complete route survives the formulation's safety guard; the native adapter maps this abstention to authority=B0_CONTROL, not to a submission fallback.
status_rules.UNSUPPORTED: Selection/effect/card semantics or public successor data is not supported, including any required Phase A PARTIAL route; the native adapter maps this abstention to authority=B0_CONTROL.
status_rules.AMBIGUOUS: Two or more non-equivalent semantic routes have identical keys; no option-order tie break is permitted. The native adapter maps this abstention to authority=B0_CONTROL.
status_rules.B0_DELEGATE: Runtime route authority abstains and invokes the frozen public B0 control. This is a route abstention/delegation, not a fallback action; only a failure of B0 or the final adapter counts as fallback.

fail_closed_matrix.response: TERMINAL_OVERRIDE in the evaluator before reading selection; no runtime action is emitted
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: Any post-terminal action is a hard reliability failure

fail_closed_matrix.condition: unknown selection enum, malformed request, missing required field or impossible source/target reference
fail_closed_matrix.response: UNSUPPORTED with authority=B0_CONTROL (runtime status B0_DELEGATE); retain compact reproduction capsule

fail_closed_matrix.condition: hidden/private field appears in route input or future-state information is observed
fail_closed_matrix.response: UNSUPPORTED with authority=B0_CONTROL and hidden_leak_rejections += 1 (runtime status B0_DELEGATE)

fail_closed_matrix.condition: required route edge depends on Riptide, Swirling Waves, Surfing Beach, Hammer-lanche or Frost Barrier behavior not proven in Phase A
fail_closed_matrix.response: UNSUPPORTED with authority=B0_CONTROL; no card-specific authority (runtime status B0_DELEGATE)
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: Candidate may remain a B0 control only; route arm cannot promote

fail_closed_matrix.condition: A has an unknown declared response or B lacks a complete finite public class/weight
fail_closed_matrix.response: A fails robust comparison; B returns UNRESOLVED; neither guesses and the native adapter delegates to B0
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: Activation is inactive, not a win/loss result

fail_closed_matrix.condition: non-equivalent key tie or semantic duplicate cannot be canonicalized
fail_closed_matrix.response: AMBIGUOUS; never select by original_index; the native adapter delegates to B0
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: Ambiguous count is reported; repeated ambiguity blocks route authority

fail_closed_matrix.condition: horizon or branch budget truncates any candidate needed for the key
fail_closed_matrix.response: NO_SAFE_ROUTE with max_horizon_pruned += 1; the native adapter delegates to B0
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: No strength conclusion from that decision

fail_closed_matrix.condition: optional STOP is not legal or multiselect count is outside min/max
fail_closed_matrix.response: Reject that action; do not synthesize STOP/empty selection
fail_closed_matrix.promotion_effect: Invalid action is a hard reliability failure

deterministic_fixtures.purpose: A forced terminal legal action outranks every non-terminal route.
deterministic_fixtures.setup: The current public observation has terminal_result set to an exact engine win/draw/loss and no usable selection request; any stale selection payload is intentionally present only in the fixture record.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: The evaluator returns TERMINAL_OVERRIDE before reading selection data; no route action is emitted. A non-terminal action whose successor later becomes terminal is evaluated only in the offline successor fixture, not by pretending the current request is terminal.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: A planner that reads select data before terminal state or treats a current non-terminal request as already terminal fails.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: A public non-terminal KO exists, no next attacker is ready, opponent has a public ready attacker and faster declared retaliation; a develop/deny option preserves a route.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: A rejects the cosmetic KO. B rejects it when the retaliation class is complete and its weight is nonzero; otherwise B is UNRESOLVED, never optimistic.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: Largest immediate Prize must not win by itself.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: High damage leaves the opponent engine/attacker intact; lower damage denies a publicly route-critical target and has a complete follow-up.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: A selects the robust denial route. B selects it unless the declared envelope genuinely gives the high-damage route a higher mean while passing its tail guard.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: Damage metadata is not a route result.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: Two actions have declared public response classes: action X has completion scores [0.9, 0.9] and action Y has [1.0, 0.2], equal weights; X worst case is better, Y mean is better.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: A selects X by worst-case robustness; B selects Y only if its lower-tail/catastrophic guard passes. The fixture must include a second Y version where 0.2 is catastrophic and B correctly rejects it.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: A and B must not collapse to one weighted score or one shared tie-break.

deterministic_fixtures.purpose: Prevent unsupported Phase A semantics becoming route authority.
deterministic_fixtures.setup: Legal options require one of 721:1042, 721:1043, 1262, 723:1046 or 723:1047 to complete the route.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: The dependent candidate is UNSUPPORTED for both arms and B0 authority remains; no guessed effect, timing or damage modifier is emitted.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: Static CSV prose and aggregate HP/deck deltas must not upgrade PARTIAL to exact.

deterministic_fixtures.purpose: Detect private baseline or hidden-card leakage.
deterministic_fixtures.setup: Two otherwise identical states differ only in an opponent hidden hand or facedown Prize identity; the route input includes no public reveal.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: Decision and route key are identical, or both requests are rejected if hidden data is supplied; no output may depend on hidden identity.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: Opponent hand/deck certainty and private-baseline coupling are prohibited.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: Permute complete legal options 32 times and duplicate a semantically equivalent option under a different original index.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: Selected canonical semantic key is unchanged. Exact semantic duplicates are grouped; non-equivalent equal keys return AMBIGUOUS.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: No first-N or index tie break.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: Mirror the same public state for acting_player 0 and 1, including ownership, source/target references and candidate win code.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: Role-relative route decision is invariant after canonical player remapping; opponent and candidate are never swapped.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: Natural seat is a diagnostic/evaluation factor, not an accidental policy perspective.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: A visible discard/reveal removes the only accessible copy of a required attacker or energy; remaining hidden slots are unknown.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: The route cannot count the inaccessible copy as live; unknown hidden availability stays unknown and may force fail-closed.

deterministic_fixtures.setup: Use an optional ordered multiselect with legal STOP and a complete min/max range; permute ordinary options.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: STOP is scored only when legal, has its own semantic action record, and replay contribution; count/range/uniqueness remain exact.
deterministic_fixtures.counterexample_protected: No implicit empty list, stale STOP, duplicate selection or option truncation.

deterministic_fixtures.purpose: Prevent bounded search from presenting an incomplete line as a win.
deterministic_fixtures.setup: A route needs one transition beyond H or exceeds branch budget, while a shorter line is incomplete but tempting.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: Candidate is NO_SAFE_ROUTE and reports max_horizon_pruned; no strength score is attributed to the planner.

deterministic_fixtures.purpose: Exercise SF-006 and DR-015 without card-effect guessing.
deterministic_fixtures.setup: Two public routes have equal terminal distance; one fills a bench slot with a visible high-Prize liability, the other preserves capacity and a live backup.
deterministic_fixtures.expected: A uses bench_liability as a later key; B uses the same public feature only after its expected route key ties.

activation_diagnostics.activation_gate: A/B may claim an active offline fixture route only when non-terminal, at least two non-equivalent legal candidates exist, all selected-key fields are public and complete, the bounded horizon is complete for those candidates, no required edge uses a Phase A PARTIAL effect, and A/B-specific response coverage is satisfied. A native runtime route may additionally activate only after the runtime-oracle gate and route-critical semantic capsules are independently passed.
activation_diagnostics.no_op_rule: If fewer than 8 route-active games or fewer than 5 percent of eligible decisions are active in the local screen, label the route arm INCONCLUSIVE/no-op and do not promote it; route-inactive decisions delegate to B0 and are not submission fallbacks. Expand only under a predeclared budget, never cherry-pick active games.

evaluation_matrix.deployment: Natural deployment with candidate seat balance. Forced actual-first/second is a separate diagnostic and cannot be mixed into the primary estimate. No paired-seed claim.

route_arm_execution_gate.reason: The current PolicyV1 runtime receives only the current observation/request, while the route formulations require bounded successor classes. All Mega Abomasnow route-critical attack/effect semantics identified in Phase A remain PARTIAL.
required_before_native_b1: exact native semantic capsules for each route-critical Abomasnow attack/effect used by the candidate
independently reviewed runtime-compatible public route oracle that does not consume future successor data
fresh-process fail-closed tests proving B0 delegation is not counted as final-adapter fallback

mechanical_canary.purpose: B0 native mechanical adapter qualification only; no B1 native route arm is permitted while route_arm_execution_gate is BLOCKED. B1 fixture suite must pass independently.

local_screen.purpose: B0 native reliability screen with equal-budget bookkeeping. A/B route arms remain offline-fixture-only until route_arm_execution_gate passes.

local_upper_screen.purpose: Only if the independent local screen review is clean; B1 route arms still require the runtime gate and this remains a non-strength screen.

prerequisites: all deterministic fixtures pass in a fresh process
local screen has zero hard reliability counters
route_arm_execution_gate is PASS for any native A/B launch

confirmation.purpose: Held-out comparison only after private Kaggle screen review and route_arm_execution_gate PASS for any native A/B arm.

statistics.delta: independent arm score minus B0 control, with retained game-level outcomes
statistics.resampling: anchor-and-candidate-seat-stratified independent bootstrap: resample candidate and B0 games independently within each (anchor, candidate_seat) cell, compute each cell score delta, then average the eight cell deltas with fixed equal weights; never pair by engine seed or trajectory
statistics.weights: equal fixed anchor-and-seat-cell weights; no replay-derived current-meta claim
statistics.power_note: At 512 games per arm, a worst-case binary-outcome approximation gives a difference standard error near 0.031, so a 95 percent lower bound above +0.02 generally requires an observed gap around +0.08 or larger. This is an intentionally demanding promotion floor, not a negative-result test: a lower bound at or below +0.02 remains unresolved rather than proof of no value.

hard_reliability_floor: zero final-adapter fallback actions (route abstentions/B0 delegations are tracked separately and are not failures)
zero timeouts, native failures, crashes and swallowed exceptions
zero NaN/Inf and zero action/replay mismatches
zero hidden-state leaks and zero manual-randomness controls
p99 route latency within the frozen B0 budget

qualification.fixture_contract: PASS required; any failure blocks native arm execution.
qualification.mechanical_canary: PASS only with every requested complete game and every hard counter zero; otherwise REJECT.
qualification.local_screen: B0 is eligible for its own native screen after independent review and zero hard counters. A/B route arms remain blocked until the runtime-oracle and route-critical semantic gates pass; after that gate, private Kaggle eligibility additionally requires zero hard counters, route activation >=8 games and >=5 percent of eligible decisions. Lower activation is INCONCLUSIVE/no-op, not a win.
qualification.private_kaggle: Screen result is NOT_REVIEWED until independent raw-ledger recalculation; it cannot authorize confirmation by itself. Bounded private Kaggle compute is already user-authorized, but no native A/B launch is technically eligible while the runtime-oracle or route-critical semantic gate is BLOCKED.

confirmation_promotion.route_activation_minimum: 32 activated decisions per arm, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE
confirmation_promotion.aggregate_delta: anchor/seat-stratified independent bootstrap 95 percent lower bound for candidate minus B0 must be strictly greater than +0.02 and point estimate must be at least B0
confirmation_promotion.anchor_floor: No anchor point estimate may be more than 0.10 below B0; any hard catastrophic matchup failure rejects the arm regardless of aggregate mean.
confirmation_promotion.winner_rule: A/B winner only if its confirmation lower bound is >+0.02, the other arm is not also independently above +0.02, and all anchor floors pass. If both pass, retain both challenger records and choose the larger preregistered score only with overlapping-interval disclosure.
confirmation_promotion.authority: A passing arm is an experimental route challenger, not a deck freeze or gold/medal claim. Separate explicit approval is required for production authority.

rejection: Any hard reliability counter is non-promotable regardless of WDL.
No activation or insufficient active decisions is INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence of no strategic value; route inactivity delegates to B0 and is not a fallback failure.
Bootstrap 95 percent upper bound below zero rejects the route challenger against B0.
Aggregate lower bound not above +0.02 retains B0 and marks the challenger unresolved.
Any per-anchor catastrophic degradation beyond the declared 0.10 floor rejects.
Any partial-effect use, hidden/private input, raw-index dependence or manual randomness rejects the arm and its evidence.
No B1 result may replace the trusted private native anchor or freeze the candidate deck.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: A route evaluator can look complete while native effect transitions remain PARTIAL.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Keep the five route-specific effects as UNSUPPORTED dependencies until the exact native upgrade tests in Phase A are independently retained.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: B's public response envelope could smuggle a hidden-state prior into the feature or be mistaken for a runtime policy input.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Keep B fixture-only in this phase; require sealed synthetic public successor classes, explicit predeclared weights and source receipts, reject missing weights, and keep RQ-009 separate. A native B arm needs a new runtime-oracle review.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: A/B appear different in synthetic fixtures but activate identically in native games.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Require F04 divergence and activation diagnostics; report no-op activation rather than claiming a formulation comparison.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: B0 and B1 share adapter or native baseline bugs, hiding regressions.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Use the same frozen native engine receipts but independently recalculate game outcomes and run 32 option permutations; never use private baseline outputs as candidate observations.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: Equal game counts do not equal equal compute if route search is slower.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Record p50/p95/p99 decision latency and cumulative per-game CPU; reject outside the declared B0 budget.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: Natural-seated observations are insufficient to separate seat from route effects.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Balance candidate seats in the primary matrix and label forced-first/second diagnostics separately.

open_risks_and_required_followups.risk: A fixed H can make a route appear worse through pruning.
open_risks_and_required_followups.mitigation: Emit max_horizon_pruned and classify affected decisions as unresolved; do not extend after seeing outcomes without a new preregistration.

next_falsifiable_work_order: 1. Independently review B0 implementation and close its mechanical canary before adding route authority.

2. Implement only the B1 offline fixture schema/evaluator in a new owned change, with F01-F12 and fresh-process permutation tests; do not modify Phase A semantics or feed fixture successors to PolicyV1.

3. Run a no-engine deterministic A/B divergence and fail-closed qualification; retain raw fixture ledger and independent recalculation, including explicit B weights as fixture configuration rather than learned priors.

4. Before any native A/B arm, retain exact route-critical semantic capsules for the Mega Abomasnow route attacks/effects and independently review a runtime-compatible public route oracle; until then native A/B activation is BLOCKED and only B0 may run native screens.
5. After the runtime gate, run equal-budget local native screen arms beside B0, with route activation, B0 delegation and hard reliability counters retained per request.

6. Once the fixed technical prerequisites are met, launch the already user-authorized bounded private Kaggle screen under this contract; no routine additional compute approval is implied, and never submit to Kaggle.
7. Treat RQ-004/RQ-005 as unresolved until held-out confirmation meets this report's predeclared thresholds.
